graded_task_tree.requirements: The core contributions of the paper have been reproduced.

sub_tasks.requirements: A convolutional neural network (CNN) has been implemented to encode the state of the ALE environments, as described in Section 4.1 and Appendix E.1.
sub_tasks.explanation: Aggregated score from sub-tasks.

sub_tasks.requirements: A CNN has been implemented and is used to encode the state of both ALE environments to a low-dimensional vector.
sub_tasks.explanation: Aggregated score from sub-tasks.

sub_tasks.requirements: The CNN has three convolutional layers with 32, 64 and 64 channels and filter sizes of 8, 4 and 3 respectively.
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: The CNN has a final dense layer with an output dimension of 512.
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: Logic to use a single CNN encoder per policy has been implemented, where the encoder for a new policy is initialized with the weights of the previous one, as described in Appendix E.2.
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: The output of the encoder is an input to both CompoNet (actor) as well as the value function (critic).
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: The CompoNet architecture has been implemented, as described in Section 4.
sub_tasks.explanation: Aggregated score from sub-tasks.

sub_tasks.requirements: A matrix $\Phi^{k;s}$ of size $(k-1) \times |A|$ is defined which stores the output vectors of all preceding $k - 1$ modules for the current state, where $k$ is the number of tasks seen so far (including the current one) and $A$ is the action space.
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: Logic to compute $h_s \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{enc}}}$ has been implemented, where $h_s$ is computed by the CNN encoder when encoding is needed (i.e., for the Arcade Learning Environment tasks) and $h_s = s$ when no encoder is needed (i.e., for the Meta-World tasks).
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: The output attention head has been implemented, as described in Section 4.2 -- "Output Attention Head".
sub_tasks.explanation: Aggregated score from sub-tasks.

sub_tasks.requirements: The logic to compute the query vector for the output attention head has been implemented.
sub_tasks.explanation: Aggregated score from sub-tasks.

sub_tasks.requirements: A parameter matrix $W_{out}^Q$ is defined with shape $d_{enc} \times d_{model}$ where $d_{enc}$ is the size of the encoded state vector and $d_{model}$ is the hidden size of the model.
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: The query vector is computed via $q = h_s W_{out}^Q$ where $h_s$ is the encoded state vector.
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: The logic to compute the key vector for the output attention head has been implemented.
sub_tasks.explanation: Aggregated score from sub-tasks.

sub_tasks.requirements: A parameter matrix $W_{out}^K$ is defined with shape $|A| \times d_{model}$ where $A$ is the action space and $d_{model}$ is the hidden size of the model.
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: A cosine positional embedding matrix $E_{out}$ of size $(k-1) \times |A|$ is defined.
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: The key vector is computed via $(\Phi^{k;s} + E_{out}) W_{out}^Q$.
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: The logic to compute the value vector for the output attention head has been implemented, which is defined as $\Phi^{k;s}$ (the matrix of outputs from all previous modules).
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: The output vector $v$ for the output attention head is computed via $\text { Attention }(\mathbf{q}, K, V)=\text{softmax}\left(\frac{q K^T}{\sqrt{d_{\text {model }}}}\right) V$.
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: The only learnable parameters for the output attention head are $W_{out}^Q$ and $W_{out}^K$.
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: The input attention head has been implemented, as described in Section 4.2 -- "Input Attention Head".
sub_tasks.explanation: Aggregated score from sub-tasks.

sub_tasks.requirements: A matrix $P$ is defined as the row-wise concatenation of the output of the previous block (i.e., the output attention head) and $\Phi^{k;s}$ (the matrix of outputs from all previous modules).
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: The logic to compute the query vector for the input attention head has been implemented.
sub_tasks.explanation: Aggregated score from sub-tasks.

sub_tasks.requirements: A parameter matrix $W_{in}^Q$ is defined with shape $d_{enc} \times d_{model}$ where $d_{enc}$ is the size of the encoded state vector and $d_{model}$ is the hidden size of the model.
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: The query vector is computed via $q = h_s W_{in}^Q$ where $h_s$ is the encoded state vector.
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: The logic to compute the key vector for the input attention head has been implemented.
sub_tasks.explanation: Aggregated score from sub-tasks.

sub_tasks.requirements: A parameter matrix $W_{in}^K$ is defined with shape $|A| \times d_{model}$ where $A$ is the action space and $d_{model}$ is the hidden size of the model.
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: A cosine positional embedding matrix $E_{in}$ of the same size as $P$ is defined.
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: The key vector is computed via $(P + E_{in}) W_{in}^K$.
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: The logic to compute the value vector for the input attention head has been implemented.
sub_tasks.explanation: Aggregated score from sub-tasks.

sub_tasks.requirements: A parameter matrix $W_{in}^V$ is defined with shape $|A| \times d_{model}$ where $A$ is the action space and $d_{model}$ is the hidden size of the model.
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: The value vector is computed via $P W_{in}^V$.
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: The output vector for the input attention head is computed via $\text { Attention }(\mathbf{q}, K, V)=\text{softmax}\left(\frac{q K^T}{\sqrt{d_{\text {model }}}}\right) V$.
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: The only learnable parameters for the input attention head are $W_{in}^Q$, $W_{in}^K$ and $W_{in}^V$.

sub_tasks.requirements: A multi-layer feed-forward block is implemented which maps a vector of length $d_{enc} + d_{model}$ to one of length $|A|$, where |A| is the dimensionality of the action space.

sub_tasks.requirements: The only learnable parameters for the internal policy are those in the multi-layer feed-forward block.
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: An $|A|$-dimension vector is computed by adding the output of the internal policy module, a vector of size $|A|$, to the output from the output attention head, the vector previously denoted as $v$.

sub_tasks.requirements: The success rate for task $i$ at timestep $t$, $p_i(t)$, is available for all timesteps and is taken as an input, which corresponds to the success rate in task $i$ at time $t$.
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: The baseline (i.e., training a randomly initialized NN for each task) success rate for each task, $p_i^b(t)$, is taken as an input, which corresponds to the success rate of the baseline method in task $i$ at time $t$.
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: The area under the success curve ($\mathrm{AUC}_i=\frac{1}{\Delta} \int_{(i-1) \cdot \Delta}^{i \cdot \Delta} p_i(t) \mathrm{d} t$) for each task is computed, as described in Equation (2) of Section 5.1.
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: The area under the baseline success curve ($\mathrm{AUC}_i^b=\frac{1}{\Delta} \int_0^{\Delta} p_i^b(t) \mathrm{d} t$) for each task is computed, as described in Equation (2) of Section 5.1.
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: The forward transfer metric $\mathrm{FTr}_i=\frac{\mathrm{AUC}_i-\mathrm{AUC}_i^b}{1-\mathrm{AUC}_i^b}$ has is computed, as described in Equation (2) of Section 5.1.
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: The reference forward transfer metric has been implemented, as described in Section 5.1 -- "Reference Forward Transfer".
sub_tasks.explanation: Aggregated score from sub-tasks.

sub_tasks.requirements: The forward transfers, $\text{FTr}(j,i)$, obtained by training a model from scratch on the $j$-th task and fine-tuning it on the $i$-th task are taken as inputs for all $i$ and $j$ such that $1 \leq j < i \leq N$.
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code for computing the reference forward transfer ($\mathrm{RT}=\frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=2}^N \max _{j<i} \mathrm{FTr}(j, i)$) has been implemented, as described in Equation (3) of Section 5.1.
sub_tasks.explanation: This is a dummy judge that always gives a score of 1.0.
